title: Areca palms (Ranong and the South)
description: Areca (betel nut) palms are mostly found in Ranong province and more broadly in southern Thailand; the distribution map also shows them in Chanthaburi/Trat, and there is a small cluster near the Myanmar border.

title: Giant milkweed clusters
description: Giant milkweed (Calotropis) can occur anywhere in Thailand but is much more common in two areas: along roadsides from northern Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) east to Surin, the largest cluster (Surin coverage is mostly from Dec 2023–Mar 2024 and very dry, while north of Korat it is much greener); and around Suphan Buri, where the landscape looks somewhat different.

title: Thai insulator ridge count
description: Count the rings on Thai 'grenade' insulators: 5–6 ridges are found throughout central Thailand (most of the country), while 7 or more ridges mean either Chiang Rai province in the far north (with mountains) or the southern peninsula. Useful e.g. in the middle of a rubber plantation.

title: Grey exposed car (Chumphon)
description: This grey exposed Google car is found in only two places: Chumphon (about 95% of the time), more precisely northern Chumphon and south-central Prachuap Khiri Khan along the coast, or Bangkok (the remaining 5%).

title: Painted pole marking around Bangkok
description: A pole marking painted white with black ink, showing one character followed by two digits, places you in Bangkok, Nonthaburi or Samut Prakan.

title: Durian orchards of Chanthaburi and Trat
description: Durian orchards (trees shaped a bit like firs, without needles) are very often in Chanthaburi and Trat provinces, about 90% of the time; look for them when the landscape feels southern and very green.

title: Oil palm plantations in the South
description: About 90% of Thailand's oil palm plantations are in the southern peninsula; oil palms mixed with rubber trees make it almost certain.

title: Wind farms at the Lopburi–Chaiyaphum–Korat tripoint
description: In central/northern Thailand there is only one area with wind turbines: around the tripoint of Lopburi, Chaiyaphum and Nakhon Ratchasima provinces.
